expected_level_description: You can: - prepare the annual accounts and statutory returns to a timetable - apply accounting standards to complex areas, such as leases, cloud computing arrangements, and intangible assets - write accounting papers that explain judgements and estimates - manage the external audit of the accounts and respond to findings
You can: - prepare daily cash positions and short-term cash forecasts - prepare payment runs and check they are properly authorised - reconcile bank accounts and clear unmatched items

You can: - test and improve the controls for a financial process - manage audit requests for an area and agree actions on findings - write and update financial procedures - work with counter-fraud specialists to reduce fraud risk
You can: - prepare tax returns and reconciliations under supervision - apply the right tax treatment to common purchases and income - check employment status for contractors under guidance

You can: - apply the organisation's capital and revenue rules to everyday spending - explain how funding allocations and spending limits affect your area - recognise spending that needs approval from a funder or spending control
You can: - use spreadsheets well, including formulas, lookups, and pivot tables - maintain finance system data, such as cost centres, suppliers, and approvers - report and help fix system problems
You can: - balance cost versus value - consider the impact of user needs - report on financial delivery - monitor cost and budget - understand how and when to escalate issues

You can: - listen to the needs of design and business stakeholders and interpret information - take part in discussions within a multidisciplinary team - be an advocate for the team externally, and can manage differing perspectives - shape and share communications relevant to the audience
